title: Cold storage, shop shelves and selling honestly

say: Cold storage, shop shelves, and selling honestly.
This is the video for module 4 of Food Preservation and Storage.
The cold chain is the unbroken line of cold from market or pot to plate. Keep your fridge below 5 degrees Celsius. Check it with a thermometer in the morning, before anyone opens the door.

panel.heading: Know your temperatures
items: Fridge: below 5°C, checked with a thermometer
Freezer: -18°C, food frozen rock hard
Cooked food out: no more than 2 hours
Raw meat and fish on the lowest shelf

say: A home freezer should be at about minus 18 degrees, with food frozen rock hard.

say: Divide a big pot of stew into shallow containers so it cools quickly, and get it into the fridge within 2 hours.

panel.heading: Cool, freeze, thaw, reheat
items: Cool stew fast in shallow containers
Freeze flat, meal-sized portions
Label every bag with name and date
Thaw in the fridge overnight
Reheat to a full boil

say: Freeze in flat, meal-sized bags. They freeze and thaw faster, and you take out only what you need.

say: In a power cut, keep the doors closed. A closed fridge keeps food safe for up to about 4 hours.

cards.d: Safe for up to about 4 hours with the door closed.
Holds for about 24 hours. A full freezer holds for about 48 hours.
Perishables at 4°C or above for over 2 hours: throw out. Ice crystals left: can refreeze.

say: A half-full freezer holds for about 24 hours, and a full one about 48. So fill empty space with bottles of water. Once frozen, they act like ice blocks.

say: Perishable food at 4 degrees or above for more than 2 hours goes in the bin, without tasting. Frozen food that still has ice crystals can be refrozen.

say: For example, Kemi in Port Harcourt loses power from 8 pm until 2 pm the next day. That is 18 hours, and nobody opened the doors.

panel.heading: Deciding after an 18-hour outage
items: Power off 8 pm to 2 pm: 18 hours
Fridge at 12°C: stew and fish thrown away
Freezer: under 24 hours, ice crystals: keep
Next time: water bottles in the freezer

say: Her fridge reads 12 degrees, far beyond the 4-hour guide. She throws away the cooked stew and fresh fish.

say: Keep bags on shelves or pallets, off the floor and away from walls, in a cool, dry place. Move opened rice, beans or garri into containers with tight lids.

panel.heading: Rotate stock: first expired, first out
items: Off the floor, away from walls, cool and dry
Chemicals on a separate shelf, below food
Check dates, dents and pests on arrival
New stock at the back, earliest date in front
Weekly check: list anything due within a month

say: Store kerosene, insecticide and bleach on a separate shelf, below food, and never in old food bottles.

say: Once a week, check every shelf. For example, Ada in Owerri found 48 packs of spaghetti but sells only 12 a week, with 3 weeks to the date. She moved them to the front counter and stopped ordering.
Covering or changing a date is dishonest and puts customers at risk.

panel.rule: Never sell food past its date, and never change a date.

say: Every pack you sell needs these six things. Set your best-before date from your own storage test, well inside the time the quality held.
If you plan to sell packaged food widely, through supermarkets or across states, it needs NAFDAC registration.

panel.heading: What your label should say
items: Product name that says what it is
Ingredients, largest amount first
Net weight or volume
Date made and best-before date
Storage instructions
Your business name and phone number

say: For example, Funmi dries 20 kg of tomatoes a month. With her drying ratio of 10, that gives 2 kg of flakes, or 20 packs of 100 g.
Tomatoes cost about 24,000 naira.
Bags cost 2,000 naira, labels 1,000, and transport 1,500.
And she values her 6 hours of work at 3,000 naira.
Full cost: 31,500 naira, or 1,575 naira a pack. She adds 40% and rounds to 2,250 naira a pack. Her price pays for her time as well as her tomatoes.
To remember. Keep the fridge cold and cooked food out for no more than 2 hours. In a power cut, keep doors closed. Rotate stock so the earliest date sells first.
Label honestly, and price from your full cost. Confirm every transfer in your own app before you hand over goods.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Fridge below 5°C; cooked food in within 2 hours
Power cut: 4, 24 and 48 hours, doors closed
FEFO: earliest date at the front
Honest label with a tested best-before date
Price from full cost, including your labour

say: Now practise. Record your fridge temperature for five days and write a household outage plan. Rotate and audit one shelf. Then price and label one product you have made, and start its storage test.
